items.text: The equation shows that you will need the same number of moles of sodium hydrogencarbonate. Therefore we know that we need 0.00250 mol of NaHCO₃}.

items.label: text
items.text: To calculate the volume this is in, we just need to rearrange our concentration equation to obtain:

items.label: formula
items.text: \text {volume} \left ( d m ^ { 3 } \right ) = \frac { \text {number of holes} \left ( m o l \right ) } { \text {concentration} \left ( m o l / d m ^ { 3 } \right ) }

items.label: text
items.text: The volume comes out in dm³ because the concentration is in mol/dm³. We can convert to cm³ by multiplying by 1000:

items.label: text
items.text: volume of NaHCO₃ solution = 25.0 cm³
